newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Motorcyling-Doohan wins Austrian grand prix.
newsitem.headline: Motorcyling-Doohan wins Austrian grand prix.

text.p: Three-times world champion Michael Doohan recorded his 38th career victory at the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday to take second place in the all-time list of 500cc winners.

Only Giacomo Agostini of Italy is still ahead of the Australian Honda rider, with 68 wins. "To have achieved 38 wins is fantastic but records are not important," said Doohan, 31. "The day will come when someone will overtake me in the list."
"My hair is already quite grey so I don't think I'll be around long enough to reach Agostini."
Doohan's fourth victory of the season extended his lead in the standings over Spanish teammate Alex Criville to 31 points.

But despite his domination this season, Doohan is not yet thinking about the championship which would make him only the third rider after Agostini and Britain's Mike Hailwood to achieve four successive titles.
"We still have a long way to go before the championship is decided," he said.
Doohan also posted the fastest lap of one minute 28.666 and broke the A1-Ring's official lap record set by last year's winner Criville in 1996.
"I didn't know Alex ran off the track until after I crossed the finish line," said Doohan. "If I would have known that then I wouldn't have clocked the fastest time in my last lap."
Criville was a close second to Doohan for most of the 28-lap race, but went off the track after an error and finished a disappointing fifth.

The mistake allowed the pair's third team mate, Tadayuki Okada of Japan, to finish second 22.077 seconds behind Doohan. Italian Luca Cadalora, on a Yamaha, was third, the only non-Honda rider in the top six.

Okada, who was an uncertain starter after he sustained an injury to his left hip in Saturday's final qualifying, was barely able to climb on the rostrum. He also injured his wrist in the Italian Grand Prix two weeks ago.
Officials said Japan's Takuma Aoki is receiving hospital treatment for concussion and chest injuries sustained in a first-lap crash.
Olivier Jacque of France won the 250cc race after overtaking Germany's Ralf Waldmann on the final lap. World champion Max Biaggi of Italy extended his lead in the standings with third place.
Japanese Honda rider Noburu Ueda took the lead in the 125cc standings from Aprilia's Valentino Rossi -- winning in 40:19.719, just 0.004 seconds ahead of the Italian.
